title: Nurse refill protocol: days' supply of a replacement fill
content:
**Protocol clause — Prescriptions & Renewals replacement fills.**

A replacement fill for lost, stolen or damaged medication dispenses one regular fill of the prescription, that is, the per-fill days' supply recorded on the prescription. The replacement fill is posted as one fill on the day it is authorized, and its days' supply is a whole number of days.

**How the replacement days are assembled.** The replacement days are worked out in this order:

1. the lost supply is counted;
2. the credit for the fills the prescription still authorizes is set against it;
3. the lost supply less the credit is multiplied by the replaced share, and any fraction of a day is dropped;
4. the follow-up trim is subtracted from that whole number of days.

The replacement days are never below zero: a result under zero is zero.

**The components.** The lost supply is one regular fill — the per-fill days' supply recorded on the prescription. The credit is 0 days. The replaced share is 100 percent. The follow-up trim is 0 days.

**Worked figures (hypothetical prescriptions).**

| Per-fill days' supply on the prescription | Lost supply | Less credit | Multiplied by the replaced share | Less trim | Replacement days |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| 90 | 90 | 90 | 90 | 90 | 90 |

**Points of judgement.**
- The per-fill days' supply is the one recorded on the prescription on the day of the replacement.
- The trim of clause 4 is subtracted from the whole number of days that clause 3 produces, and is not itself multiplied by the share.
- The figure passed as the replacement fill's days' supply is a whole number of days.
